findings.checklist_item: State the explicit mapping from each find_similar failure branch (:63-64, :67-72, :83-85) to its status value, and confirm the 'any other exception' branch is intentionally labeled provider-error.
evidence: Plan lists statuses: 'records a `status` from the closed set `ok`, `index-absent`, `catch-up-failed`, `provider-error`'
Plan describes three failure branches: absent index `[]` (:63-64), catch-up failure warns then `[]` (:67-72), 'any other exception warns then `[]` (:83-85)'
AC: 'When the embedding provider errors, `coverage["overlap"]["status"]` is `provider-error`' — but :83-85 is a generic 'any other exception', not specifically a provider error
findings.finding: The plan defines a four-value closed status set {ok, index-absent, catch-up-failed, provider-error} but never states which of find_similar's three internal failure branches maps to which non-ok status; in particular the branch described as 'any other exception warns then []' (:83-85) must be the one labeled 'provider-error', yet the AC tests a specifically 'embedding provider' error against that status.
findings.location: Approach -> 'Diagnostic contract' and 'The one gap: failure distinguishability'; ACs 'provider-error'
scenarios: Executor wires status recording and must decide whether a non-provider exception at :83-85 is labeled provider-error or a distinct value
A reviewer reads provider-error for an exception that had nothing to do with the embedding provider
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to the Diagnostic contract: ':63-64 absent index -> index-absent; :67-72 catch-up failure -> catch-up-failed; :83-85 any other exception (the embedding/provider path being the only remaining error source) -> provider-error.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the 'provider-error' status with find_similar's verified behavior: rank converts provider failures (TierUnavailable) to a None degrade so find_similar returns non-empty LEXICAL results, making provider-error indistinguishable from unconfigured and never []; either surface the provider-error signal from rank into diagnostics, or drop the provider-error status and its two ACs and re-state degradation as 'lexical fallback on provider failure'.
evidence: Plan: 'find_similar collapses every failure to an empty list -- ... any other exception warns then [] (:83-85)' and defines closed status set including 'provider-error'

embedding.py:125-132 (TierUnavailable docstring): 'Raised internally and converted to a degrade by rank; it never reaches a find_similar caller.' and '"not configured" from "configured and failing" ... both produce lexical results.'

similar/__init__.py:79-82: 'ranked = embedding_rank(...)' then 'if ranked is not None: return ranked; return search(...)' -- a provider failure makes rank return None, so find_similar returns the LEXICAL search() result, which is non-empty when the index has matches, not [].

This contradicts the AC that provider-error yields an EMPTY injected candidate set / overlap finding set empty: with lexical fallback the candidate list is non-empty and overlap findings CAN be emitted.
findings.finding: The plan's premise 'find_similar collapses every failure to an empty list' and its proposed 'provider-error' status are refuted by the code: a provider/embedding failure is converted inside rank to a None degrade and find_similar falls through to NON-EMPTY lexical results, never to [].
findings.location: Approach -> 'The one gap: failure distinguishability' / 'Diagnostic contract'; AC 'When the embedding provider errors ... status is provider-error ... with the overlap finding set empty'
scenarios: Embedding tier configured with credentials that error at query time; the index exists and has matching tickets
Author implements diagnostics in find_similar expecting a distinguishable provider-error path

claimability.py:127-140: coverage_extra is a parameter of indeterminate_verdict, whose docstring scopes it to 'the non-LLM early returns (not-claimable fast-fail, plan-relation-snapshot error)' with coverage.llm_ran=false

By the plan's own 'Degradation' / AC design, overlap runs during a normal LLM review (llm_ran true), not an early-return INDETERMINATE
findings.finding: The 'Recording channel' section names the wrong edit target: coverage['overlap'] cannot be recorded via the coverage_extra seam at claimability.py:132/:153, because that seam (indeterminate_verdict's coverage_extra parameter) is reached ONLY on the LLM-skipping early-return INDETERMINATE paths (not_claimable :120, plan_relation_snapshot_error __init__.py:392, retry_refused retry.py:168). The overlap path runs through run_pass1, which writes coverage in place.

scenarios: Implementing the acceptance criteria that assert coverage['overlap']['status'] == index-absent / catch-up-failed / provider-error on a normal (non-early-return) review
findings.suggested_fix: Name the run_pass1 coverage mutation (the dict seeded at production_batch_runner.py:134, mutated in pass1.py like coverage['chunks']) as the recording channel for coverage['overlap']; drop the claimability.py coverage_extra reference, which belongs to the early-return INDETERMINATE verdicts.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name how the `provider-error` status is distinguished from an unconfigured/absent embedding tier, given `embedding.rank` returns a single undifferentiated `None`; either scope a `rank` diagnostic-surface change or narrow the closed set to the statuses actually distinguishable at the `find_similar` boundary.
evidence: Plan: find_similar 'records a status from the closed set ok, index-absent, catch-up-failed, provider-error' and proposes adding `diagnostics: dict | None` only to find_similar

src/rebar/similar/embedding.py:418-424: rank's docstring — 'None is the single degrade signal, and every unavailability shares it: no configured model, an absent optional backend, a provider denial or timeout, and a corpus without full current-key coverage... the distinction is carried in the diagnostic rather than in the return value' (the 'diagnostic' is a log line/exception message, not a returned structured status)
src/rebar/similar/embedding.py:430-435: both TierUnavailable and generic Exception return None — no cause crosses the return boundary
src/rebar/similar/__init__.py:79-81: find_similar sees only `ranked is not None`, so it cannot label provider-error vs unconfigured
Absence rationale: the plan proposes no change to embedding.rank's surface and states 'add no second retrieval path' / find_similar is 'its whole public surface'
findings.finding: The `provider-error` diagnostic status is not achievable as described: `find_similar` cannot distinguish a provider error from an unconfigured/absent embedding tier, because `embedding.rank` collapses all degradation causes (provider denial/timeout, no model configured, absent backend, incomplete coverage) into a single `None` return by design and exposes no structured cause to the caller.
findings.location: Approach → 'Diagnostic contract' (closed set includes `provider-error`); ACs 'When the embedding provider errors, coverage["overlap"]["status"] is provider-error'
scenarios: Install with an embedding model configured whose provider times out/denies during an overlap review — find_similar receives None indistinguishable from the common 'no model configured' case, so it cannot set status=provider-error
Install with no embedding tier configured — same None, so provider-error and the unconfigured case cannot be told apart

So overlap rides req.with_inputs -- the seam already carrying probe_criteria (:123) and relation_snapshot (:157) -- set where the batch request is assembled"

gates/plan-review.yaml declares `probe_criteria` as a workflow input (lines 24-30) and maps `probe_criteria: ${{ inputs.probe_criteria }}` into the finders batch step `with:` (lines 54,66) — this is what populates req.with_inputs via interpreter.py:386-397 `BatchRunRequest(..., with_inputs=resolved_with)`
production_batch_runner.py:123 reads `req.with_inputs.get("probe_criteria")` — the READ end only, downstream of all the omitted hops

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify which Pass-1 chunk receives the overlap block and which criterion id the advisory overlap finding is attributed to (or define a dedicated overlap criterion/pseudo-id that _chunk_extra_context gates on), so injection and finding-attribution are deterministic.
evidence: pass1.py:219-222 gates each context block on `any(c.get('id') == 'G5' ...)` / `'no-file-impact'`, so a block rides the chunk carrying that criterion and is judged by that criterion's finder
The P1Finding schema requires `criteria[]` ids (passes.py:60-77); an overlap finding emitted by an arbitrary chunk's finder would be attributed to that chunk's criterion ids
The plan states overlap 'rides a chunk already being sent' and 'the existing Pass-1 unit does the judging' but names no chunk/criterion
findings.finding: The plan does not specify which Pass-1 chunk the `## POSSIBLE OVERLAP` block attaches to, nor which criterion id the resulting advisory finding maps to. Overlap is not a criterion in the single/agent set, yet the existing _chunk_extra_context gates each injected block on a criterion's presence in the chunk (e.g. any(id=='G5'), 'no-file-impact'), and the gated criterion's finder is what judges the injected context and owns the emitted finding's criteria[].
findings.location: Approach: 'Ride the existing Pass-1 extra-context seam' and 'The existing Pass-1 unit does the judging'; pass1.py:_chunk_extra_context:215-223
scenarios: overlap=True with chunk ordering/partition varying across runs: the block could land in different chunks, making the injected-candidate count (AC2) and context_digest nondeterministic
A downstream severity/verdict step that keys on a finding's criteria[] receives an overlap finding tagged with an unrelated chunk's criterion id
findings.suggested_fix: Gate the overlap block on a stable, always-present chunk (or introduce an `overlap` pseudo-criterion id that is added to one chunk when overlap=True and used as the finding's criteria[] tag), mirroring how G5/no-file-impact bind their blocks to a named criterion.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the exact chunk/criterion that the '## POSSIBLE OVERLAP (from store)' block attaches to in `_chunk_extra_context` (mirroring the `c.get('id')=='G5'` gate), so the overlap directive is co-located with a single owning finder rather than broadcast to every chunk.
evidence: Plan: 'Candidates ride a chunk already being sent, so overlap judging adds no LLM call' and 'Appending candidates there' — but no criterion gate is named.
Code: `_chunk_extra_context` injects decomp_context only `if any(c.get('id') == 'G5' for c in chunk)` (pass1.py:219); the no-file-impact block is similarly gated (pass1.py:221).

If appended to every chunk, every criterion finder receives an overlap directive unrelated to its own criterion — an instruction-locality / pink-elephant antipattern; if appended to one chunk, that chunk is unnamed.
findings.finding: The overlap block's host chunk/criterion is unspecified: the mirrored decomposition_state_block is injected into ONLY the chunk carrying G5 (pass1.py:219 gates on `c.get('id')=='G5'`), but the plan never names which criterion/chunk the overlap directive attaches to in _chunk_extra_context.
findings.location: Approach — 'Ride the existing Pass-1 extra-context seam' / 'Zero marginal LLM cost' and pass1.py:215-223
scenarios: A reviewer implements the seam and must guess whether overlap rides G5's chunk, a new dedicated chunk, or all chunks — each choice changes which finder judges overlap and the checkpoint topology.
findings.suggested_fix: Gate the overlap injection on a specific criterion id (the one whose finder is designated to judge overlap), exactly as decomp_context is gated on G5, and state that id in the plan.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the `criteria[]` rubric id the advisory overlap finding carries (introduce/name the finder criterion), distinct from epic 62dc's source 'criterion 5'.
evidence: Plan directive: 'emit one advisory finding per overlapping candidate naming its id and why'.
Pass-1 findings are keyed by rubric id (`criteria[]`) — e.g. budget-shed records set `'criteria': [c['id']]` (pass1.py:273) and `decomposition_state_block` targets the G5 finder.
No criterion id is assigned to the overlap finding; 'criterion 5' refers to epic 62dc, not a plan-review finder criterion.
findings.finding: The rubric/criteria id the emitted advisory overlap finding carries is never defined. Pass-1 findings carry a `criteria[]` of rubric ids, but the plan names only epic 62dc 'criterion 5' (a source requirement, not a finder criterion id) for a finding the LLM is told to 'emit one advisory finding per overlapping candidate'.
findings.location: Approach — 'The injected block carries its decision rule' and Acceptance Criteria (overlap finding)
scenarios: Downstream routing/affirmation/severity passes consume `criteria[]`; an overlap finding with an undefined or absent criterion id cannot be classified or deduplicated against the finder set.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the fallback-failure disposition for overlap retrieval: say whether a `provider-error` (embedding tier) preserves the lexical-tier leg or degrades to empty, and give each arm (index-absent / catch-up-failed / provider-error) an explicit disposition word so the most-recoverable leg is never masked.
evidence: 'With the optional embedding tier configured it ranks through that tier, otherwise lexically (`:79-82`)'
'any other exception warns then `[]` (`:83-85`)' mapped to status `provider-error`
'On any non-`ok` status the candidate list is empty and no overlap finding is emitted'

ABSENCE: the plan never says whether a `provider-error` (embedding tier fails but the lexical tier is present) falls back to the lexical leg or discards it, and never classifies the arms with a disposition word (transient/retryable vs fatal/permanent).
findings.finding: The plan adds a diagnostics contract over find_similar's embedding-vs-lexical fallback chain but does not state the fallback-failure winner: on 'provider-error' it degrades the whole retrieval to an empty candidate set (mapping the embedding-tier exception to `[]`), which discards the still-available lexical-tier leg rather than preserving the most-recoverable leg. A transient/retryable embedding-provider throttle would thus mask the lexical results that could still have been injected.
scenarios: Embedding tier configured; the embedding call throttles/errors transiently (retryable) while the lexical FTS5 index is present and would have returned candidates -> status becomes `provider-error`, candidate set is empty, no overlap finding emitted, even though lexical candidates were available and the error was transient.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Failure-disposition line: index-absent and catch-up-failed are terminal-empty (permanent for this run, non-blocking); provider-error should prefer the lexical leg's candidates when the lexical tier is available (preserving the most-recoverable leg) and only degrade to empty when no tier can answer — stating that the review verdict is unaffected in every arm.
